DIAGNOSIS READY: Huntington's Disease

The combination of subcortical dementia (forgetfulness), psychiatric symptoms (irritability, hallucinations), chorea (implied by involuntary movements), and dysphagia in a patient with a strong family history of suicide at age 50 is highly suggestive of Huntington's disease. Could you confirm if you have noticed any uncontrolled, jerky movements in your limbs or face, or if you have lost interest in activities you once enjoyed? Additionally, has anyone in your direct line of descent (parents, siblings, children) been diagnosed with a similar condition before age 60?
